headline: OpenAI treats GPT-6.2 Astra as shipped in a distillation note; Claude-assisted Riemann Lean archive typechecks

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's eleven o'clock UTC on Saturday, November twenty-first. This is ARA AI News, and today OpenAI is writing about GPT six point two as a model it already ships.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: OpenAI posted a November twentieth research note on combatting adversarial distillation, and it names GPT six point two Astra and Sol as the models that received the tighter safeguard stack.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The note argues that exact chain-of-thought traces can transfer dual-use cyber skill even from allowed coding and defense tasks. In an internal adaptive red-team, recovering protected reasoning fell from fifty-four percent on GPT six Astra to zero point two percent on GPT six point two Astra.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That comparison is OpenAI testing OpenAI, not an outside lab. A companion MedChemBench post scores GPT six point two Astra at eighty-four point five percent, just above GPT six Astra at eighty-three point three percent, with GPT six point one Sol at eighty-two percent and GPT five point six Sol at fifty-eight point two percent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: MedChemBench is ninety-nine problems from papers and patents. Structure reconstruction is the easy slice, while compound selection and numerical property prediction sit near half credit.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Trending copy that six point two tops robotics and chemistry overstates what OpenAI actually published. This is not a launch thread, and there is still no dedicated product page or API pricing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: What changed is first-party confirmation. The six point two stack is the one OpenAI is hardening, not a rumor from a podcast title.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The other new fact is mathematical, and it is not settled. Levent Alpöge posted a Lean archive he says is a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, and he says a readable paper is not ready.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: He dates the discovery to Sunday night, says the method extends to the generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, and says he messaged Dario Amodei about announcing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Anthropic's account has still not mentioned the claim. Overnight, Elliot Arledge reported compiling all one hundred seventy-five thousand one hundred eighty-seven reachable files on stock Lean four point thirty-three point one.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That compile covered more than seventeen million lines, pinned five theorems to unmodified Mathlib, and replayed a sixty-one point five seven gigabyte proof closure into the independent Rust kernel nanoda with zero errors.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Elon Musk posted this morning that even if the Riemann Hypothesis turns out not to be fully solved yet, it will be soon enough. That is a hedge, not an endorsement.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The Lean artifact exists and an independent compile is documented. The Millennium Prize claim is not settled, and Alpöge has not published a human-readable proof.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: One quieter thread is leaving the board. Black Forest Labs' Flux three robotics storyline has had no first-party revenue figure or ship date since that Latent Space episode, so we are marking it settled for now.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Watch next for a real GPT six point two product or API page, and for an independent lab repeating that reasoning-extraction eval. On the math claim, watch for an Anthropic statement or a serious critique of Mathlib's Riemann Hypothesis statement.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
